title: docs: make mem:<name> pointers in plan steps the standard, and retire a task's Serena handoff when QA approves it
description:
Requested by the human on 2026-10-30 after a governor audit of Serena usage, covering Serena logs for 10-27 to 10-30: 980 Serena sessions and 4,112 tool calls.

What works: architects already write `mem:<name>` pointers into plan steps, for example `mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate` and `mem:gotcha-proxy-npm-test-shared-checkout-deletes-dist`, so workers read exactly the right memory. That is why only 82 of 980 sessions needed list_memories. It is done ad hoc, though; no role doc asks for it.

What leaks: task-<id>-handoff memories never get retired. 304 of 349 belong to DONE or ARCHIVED tasks, and nothing in the lifecycle removes them.

Change, keeping the role docs inside npm run lint's 40-line cap for architect/worker/qa .md, with the detail in the .reference.md files and docs/MEMORY.md:
1. Architect (docs/roles/architect.md, plus the moe-planning skill where plan steps are described): when a Serena memory bears on a step, name it in that step as `mem:<name>` instead of expecting workers to scan list_memories.
2. QA (docs/roles/qa.md / qa.reference.md): after moe.qa_approve, fold anything reusable from the task's handoff into a gotcha-/pattern-/decision- memory, then retire the handoff. Archive it into .serena/memories/_archive/, which the companion cleanup task hides from list_memories through ignored_memory_patterns, or delete it if nothing reusable remains. A rejected task keeps its handoff.
3. docs/MEMORY.md: document the handoff lifecycle (written while the task is open, retired at QA approval), the `_archive/` convention, and the `mem:` pointer convention.

Role docs reach running seats only after the daemon is rebuilt, because .moe/roles is re-synced at daemon boot, and after a plugin rebuild for IDE users. Say so in the completion summary.
definitionOfDone: docs/roles/architect.md (or the moe-planning skill it points to) tells architects to name relevant Serena memories in plan steps as `mem:<name>`. docs/MEMORY.md describes the convention.

docs/roles/qa.md / qa.reference.md tell QA, after qa_approve, to fold reusable facts from task-<id>-handoff into a gotcha/pattern/decision memory and then retire the handoff (archive to .serena/memories/_archive/, or delete). A rejected task keeps its handoff. docs/MEMORY.md documents this lifecycle.

`npm run lint` at the repo root passes (the 40-line cap holds), the daemon prebuild still regenerates initFiles.ts and skillFiles.ts cleanly, and the completion summary notes that seats pick the change up at the next daemon or plugin rebuild.

implementationPlan.description:
QA RETIREMENT RULE in docs/roles/qa.md: at most 3 lines, keeping the file at or under the 40-line lint cap (32 now). This is the always-loaded QA doc; the full lifecycle goes in docs/MEMORY.md in step 3. Add a short '## Handoff retirement' section, or append to '## Approval bar', carrying the rule:

- After `moe.qa_approve` only, fold any reusable fact from this task's `task-<id>-handoff` / `task-<id>-qa-handoff` memories into a gotcha-/pattern-/decision- memory. Prefer edit_memory over a near-duplicate.
- Then retire them with a plain file move: `mkdir -p .serena/memories/_archive && mv .serena/memories/task-<id>-*handoff.md .serena/memories/_archive/`. Serena refuses `_archive/` names, so never use rename_memory. Alternatively use delete_memory when nothing is reusable and no live memory cites it.
- Write no new qa-handoff on approve.
- After `moe.qa_reject`, keep the handoffs. Never retire another task's.
- Point to docs/MEMORY.md for the lifecycle.

.serena/ is untracked and excluded at landing by both wrappers: never declare_files or commit it.

Error handling: if the move fails (missing file, existing archive copy), say so in the qa_approve summary. Never overwrite an archived file.
implementationPlan.note: QA fix for qa.md:22. Plain `mv` is replaced by a subshell that checks every `_archive/<name>` destination first and exits 1 on any collision, so nothing is retired; only then does it run `mv -n`, which backstops a race. Scratch tests: no collision moves both handoffs (exit 0); one collision exits 1, moves neither file, and the archive still reads OLD; no match exits 1 with 'cannot stat'. The `mv -n` alone is not enough: Git Bash's coreutils 8.32 `mv -n` skips with exit 0, and only 9.4 exits 1. The doc now says never use a plain mv. qa.md is 35 lines (cap 40), and the edited line is ASCII.

QA fix for MEMORY.md:80. The `_archive/` convention now carries the same check-then-move command as qa.md; the two backtick spans are byte-identical (checked by grep). It also explains why a plain `mv` is forbidden (it silently overwrites) and why `mv -n` alone isn't enough (8.32 exits 0, 9.4 exits 1), and says a non-zero exit leaves every file in place and must be reported. I ran the doc's literal command with <id> substituted. On a collision it exited 1: neither file moved, the archive kept OLD. On a clean run it exited 0: both of this task's handoffs moved, another task's handoff stayed. The added line is ASCII (the 7 non-ASCII lines were already at HEAD). MEMORY.md is not vendored, so it needs no generator.

NEVER run npm run build or prebuild in the shared tree: `clean` deletes dist/ from under other sessions. The CRLF and LF warnings are pre-existing autocrlf noise.

Error handling: if the diff carries a foreign hunk (a peer's dirty doc), restore the saved copy, name the hunk in the step note and coordinate before retrying.

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial self-review. (a) The rules agree: retire only after approve, keep on reject, use the _archive/ path, never rename_memory. The qa.md and MEMORY.md commands are byte-identical; SKILL.md is unchanged. (b) qa.md has 35 lines; architect.md and qa.reference.md are untouched (empty diff). (c) Nothing tells an agent to edit .moe or commit .serena. (d) The generated diff is only qa.md's entry, and skillFiles.ts is byte-identical. (e) The added lines are ASCII. Failure modes I checked: an unsubstituted `<id>` is a bash syntax error that exits 2 and moves nothing; a wrong cwd makes the subshell's cd fail with exit 1 and nothing moved; a glob over a full 32-hex id can't match another task. One theoretical race: if a same-name archive file appears between the pre-check and `mv -n`, 8.32 would skip it with exit 0 and leave the source unretired (not overwritten). That needs two seats retiring the same task at once, so I left it as a note. Diff vs HEAD: qa.md +1/-1, MEMORY.md +1/-1, initFiles.ts +3/-3.

reopenReason:
DoD 2's retirement command overwrites an existing archive. docs/roles/qa.md:22 and docs/MEMORY.md:80 both say to run `mkdir -p .serena/memories/_archive && mv .serena/memories/task-<id>-*handoff.md .serena/memories/_archive/` and, in the same sentence, never overwrite an archived file and report a failed move. On GNU coreutils 9.4, plain `mv` onto an existing `_archive/<same name>.md` exits 0 and replaces the archived bytes (reproduced: archive content changed from OLD to NEW). `mv -n` on the same binary exits 1, prints `not replacing`, and leaves the archive and the source in place. A multi-file `mv -n` can still move the non-colliding names; check each destination before moving so a collision retires nothing. Update both lines, regenerate initFiles.ts only (Windows Git Bash `npm run generate-init-files`; no build/prebuild; MEMORY.md is not vendored; leave skillFiles.ts alone unless SKILL.md changes), and re-run the step-5 command.

Everything else checked out. Re-ran task.verification: exit 0. lint OK (architect 39, worker 30, qa 35). tsc clean. 4 files / 38 tests passed. Both greps matched. Completion 4d6b371 is on moe/work-2026-10-24 (tree ef7e6d83, ancestor of origin/moe/work-2026-10-24 at 8d977add). Non-board +21/-5, net 16. architect.md and qa.reference.md untouched. Generated diffs are only the qa.md entry and the moe-planning marker plus two bullets. Added text is ASCII. moe-planning has the `mem:<name>` rule and architect.md still points at that skill. MEMORY.md has the lifecycle, `_archive/` convention, and pointer rule. `.serena/project.yml` has `ignored_memory_patterns: [_archive/.*]`. Completion summary names the daemon and plugin rebuild. Ponytail: lean already, net 0.
